import pandas as pd

# Load the time_series_data.csv dataset
df_time_series = pd.read_csv('/data/time_series_data.csv')

# Extract the 'CE' and 'Depot' columns
ce_values = df_time_series['CE']
depot_values = df_time_series['Depot']

# Identify the index of the maximum 'Depot' value
max_depot_index = depot_values.idxmax()

# Find the corresponding 'CE' value
peak_ce = ce_values[max_depot_index]

# Determine the century
peak_century = peak_ce // 100

peak_century

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the time_series_data.csv dataset
df_time_series = pd.read_csv('/data/time_series_data.csv')

# Extract the 'CE' and 'Depot_inter' columns
ce_values = df_time_series['CE']
depot_inter_values = df_time_series['Depot_inter']

# Plot the interpolated Depot values over time
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
plt.plot(ce_values, depot_inter_values, label='Depot Interpolated')
plt.xlabel('CE (Common Era)')
plt.ylabel('Depot Interpolated Z Values')
plt.title('Depot Interpolated Z Values Over Time')
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True)
plt.show()
